notes: Customer profile: mid-stage SMB building a chat-first support product; heavy use of embeddings for KB search but currently using hosted text generation for chat responses.
Primary pain: latency spikes at p95/p99 affecting perceived app responsiveness. Typical expectation: 120-250ms for short replies; current median ~230ms but p95 up to 800ms.
Observed patterns: traffic concentrated 09:00-18:00 PT (us-west). They are using us-west-2 region because of proximity to their infra but suspect contention on GPU pools.

SE notes from call: prompts include 2x long system messages + full customer chat context (avg 900-1,400 tokens). Candidate optimizations: compress system instructions, move static context to server-side prefix caching, use embeddings for retrieval + short template for response generation.

Recommended quick wins provided by SE: 1) Try hosted_api in us-east-1 for lower backend contention; 2) enable streaming in client and lower client timeout to 10s with graceful partial-render; 3) set max_tokens to conservative value and truncate user context to last 6 messages; 4) enable prefix caching for repetitive system prompt (SE can provision config sample).
Customer quote on call: 'Users abandon the chat when they wait more than 500ms — even small hiccups kill conversion.'
Security: they require SOC2 and SAML SSO for team admin access; retention controls asked but ok to start on hosted with standard retention while they evaluate Dedicated later.

Cost sensitivity: SMB budget conscious — prefers suggestions that don't require Dedicated immediately. Interested in batching/response trimming and region routing before committing to reserved capacity.
